question: State the law of variable proportions and explain its three stages. In which stage will a rational producer operate?
sources: Law of variable proportions (standard microeconomic theory of production, short run)

points.label: Statement and assumptions
points.description: In the short run, when more units of a variable factor are combined with fixed factors, total product first rises at an increasing rate, then at a diminishing rate, and finally falls; it assumes fixed technology, homogeneous units and at least one fixed factor.
points.basis: Law of variable proportions: statement and assumptions

points.label: Stage I: increasing returns
points.description: Total product rises; average product rises and reaches its maximum where it equals marginal product. The fixed factor is under-used.
points.basis: Law of variable proportions: stage I

points.label: Stage II: diminishing returns
points.description: Total product rises at a diminishing rate and reaches its maximum; marginal and average product both fall, and the stage ends where marginal product is zero.
points.basis: Law of variable proportions: stage II

points.label: Stage III: negative returns
points.description: Total product falls and marginal product becomes negative, as the variable factor is too much for the fixed factor.
points.basis: Law of variable proportions: stage III

points.label: Rational stage
points.description: A rational producer operates in Stage II, because in Stage I output can still be raised by adding the variable factor and in Stage III marginal product is negative.
points.basis: Law of variable proportions: stage of operation
